newsitem.title: USA: Magellan raises stock holdings, cuts bonds.
newsitem.headline: Magellan raises stock holdings, cuts bonds.

text.p: Fidelity Investments said Thursday its Magellan Fund, the nation's largest mutual fund, raised its holdings in stocks and cut its bond holdings.

In his second month at the helm, portfolio manager Bob Stansky boosted the fund's stock holdings to 82.8 percent of the portfolio at the end of July from 79.0 percent at the same time in June, according to Fidelity's Internet site (http://www.fid-inv.com).
He trimmed Magellan's holdings in bonds to 15.6 percent of assets at the end of July from 18.1 percent the previous month.
The company also said the assets of the Magellan Fund rose to $51.683 billion at the end of August and to $51.913 billion on Sept. 4 from $50.972 billion at the end of July.
However, at least one analyst said investors continued to redeem shares in the massive mutual fund, though at a slower pace than in recent months.
Eric Kobren, publisher of Fidelity Insight, said he estimated that investors redeemed $580 million to $600 million in August, "which was less than what we saw in May, June or July."
"I think we're pretty safe that assets will stabilise here," Kobren said. "Investors should sort of sit tight and not pay as much attention to it as the media does."

Kobren estimated that investors have redeemed $3.9 billion from Magellan since April and a total of $2.4 billion year-to-date as news of the fund's recent poor performance and change in fund managers became widely reported.
The closely-watched mutual fund raised its holdings in energy stocks, its largest sector holding, to 13.8 percent of assets at the end of July from 13.5 percent at the end of June.

Stocks in durables rose to 10.8 percent from 10.4 percent, industrial machinery and equipment remained unchanged at 9.2 percent, finance rose to 7.0 percent from 6.6 percent and utilities slipped to 6.8 percent from 7.1 percent, it said.
Stocks in basic industries edged up to 6.1 percent from 6.0 percent, technology rose to 5.5 percent from 3.7 percent and retail remained unchanged at 4.8 percent, Fidelity said.
Stocks in construction remained unchanged at 3.2 percent.

U.S. Treasury bonds and notes remained at the top of Magellan's top 10 holdings, however the fund dropped AT&T Corp. and a 30-year bond paying 7.625 percent from the list and added Royal Dutch Petroleum Co. and Exxon Corp.
Holdings of convertible bonds and convertible preferred stocks remained unchanged at 0.1 percent of assets.
